items.label: Navitas Q2 FY2026 (07-27-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CALL — THE FOUR 800V INFLECTION POINTS (and the answer to the 'Kyber cancelled / 800V delayed' chatter)

set.signal: CALL — CEO Chris Allexandre's FOUR 800V INFLECTION POINTS: (1) second-half 2026 ramp, accelerating in first-half 2027: SiC replaces silicon in AC/DC PSUs on power scaling and density requirements independent of the 800 V DC initiatives, 'even with 50 V DC output' — 'the growth is happening now'; (2) ramping mid-2027: the 800 V busbar in the power sidecar rack — AC/DC power shelves and BBUs move from the IT rack to the sidecar with 800 V DC output, adding high-voltage SiC in higher-power AC/DC PSUs (18 kW, 23 kW, 27 kW, 30 kW) plus new SiC and GaN content in DC/DC PSUs (15 kW-30 kW) and BBUs; Navitas is in advanced system design and large-quantity system-level reliability testing with several key customers, across multiple platforms, multiple hyperscalers and multiple merchant-power vendors per hyperscaler; the CEO said the sidecar 800 V or ±400 V (more attached to some ASICs and XPUs) 'is going to ramp earlier next year', with SiC programs ramping in the first half of next year; (3) ramping mid-to-late 2027, accelerating in late 2027 and early 2028: native 800 V — high-density DC/DC conversion integrated into GPU and XPU trays using GaN for switching frequency and power density. Asked about 800 V timing, the CEO declined to comment on NVIDIA's plans and said 'there is a misconception in the 800 V being a digital switch' — the ramp 'will happen in steps throughout 2027, of course, accelerate in 2028', not one customer — and answered 'no' on whether this changes Navitas' outlook; (4) 2028 and beyond: solid-state transformers converting mid-voltage AC from the grid directly to 800 V DC — 'the big jump is SST' in 2028, with BESS, PCS and solar starting to ramp in 2027. CFO Tonya Stevens: AI infrastructure grew 'at over 50% quarter-on-quarter, both in Q1 and in Q2, and we expect it to accelerate.' CEO: record book-to-bill, backlogs extending beyond 2026; some platforms use both GaN and SiC (DC/DC PSUs and BBUs).

items.reason: Removes the analyst's framing (the 'Kyber cancelled / 800V delayed' claim came from Needham's question; the CEO declined to comment on NVIDIA's plans) and restores speaker attribution: the AI-infrastructure growth figure was the CFO's, the inflection points the CEO's.
items.evidence: Of course, I'm not going to comment on NVIDIA and Kyber plan. ... I think there is a misconception in the 800 V being a digital switch.

items.signal_prefix: CALL — SECOND SiC SOURCE, ULTRA-HIGH-VOLTAGE ROADMAP, AND LITIGATION

set.signal: CALL — SECOND SiC SOURCE, ULTRA-HIGH-VOLTAGE ROADMAP, AND LITIGATION: CEO Chris Allexandre: Navitas announced a strategic partnership for Magnachip to license its GeneSiC Gen4 and Gen5 trench-assisted planar technology (1.2 kV, 2.3 kV, 3.3 kV and higher voltage), to be fully qualified and internalized in Magnachip's fab in South Korea — purpose: expanded adoption of Navitas SiC technology in markets Navitas does not serve and, longer term, another foundry source of Navitas SiC wafers ('We're not creating competitor, we're creating an extension of Navitas'), as the CEO sees SiC 'growing at a 60%-70% CAGR in the context of data center and grid'. Roadmap: planned third-quarter release of the new 6.5 kV SiC technology; next-generation 10 kV SiC devices in development with a prominent lead customer (announcement expected in coming weeks); the 1.2 kV JFET line (eFuse, ORing, solid-state circuit breakers) 'will add nearly $1 billion of SAM by 2030' (the CEO added that $1.3 billion of SAM by 2030 has even been referred to) — for one SST customer, offering 1.2 kV up to 3.3 kV JFETs meant 'the SAM that we could capture in that SST went up by 40%'. Manufacturing: GlobalFoundries 8-inch GaN lead parts on track for full customer sampling and qualification before year-end, initial qualified product expected in early 2027 (U.S.-based GaN manufacturing); buffer capacity secured at TSMC 'to ensure a smooth transition for existing customers throughout 2029 and beyond' (CFO Tonya Stevens: inventory $19.5 million, up $4.6 million sequentially, plus an approximately $15 million increase in Q2 prepaid expenses for wafers to be received in future quarters). Balance sheet (CFO): cash and cash equivalents $557 million; 'the company continues to have no debt'; the $203 million non-cash charge for the October 2021 business-combination earn-out was fully recognized and settled by the end of Q2. Litigation (CEO, citing the public record): Wolfspeed sued Navitas for patent infringement in both GaN and SiC; 'Two weeks later, just last week' Renesas sued Navitas; 'based on the public record, Renesas would own up to 39% of Wolfspeed'; CEO: 'this is the last step in a campaign of harassment and intimidation through litigation and looks like a desperate move' and 'You don't start litigation like this if you are winning market share'; Navitas will defend itself.

items.reason: Drops financing terms (the ~$373M raise and its $21.89 average price); fixes the timing ('Two weeks later', not a week later); restores the CEO's hedge on Renesas' stake ('would own up to 39%', 'based on the public record'); TSMC buffer is for a transition 'throughout 2029 and beyond'; attributes CEO / CFO.
items.evidence: Two weeks later, just last week, okay, Wednesday, Renesas sued us. ... based on the public record, Renesas would own up to 39% of Wolfspeed.
